newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Mercosur leaders look to firm up common stance on free trade.
newsitem.headline: Mercosur leaders look to firm up common stance on free trade.

text.p: Leaders from the Mercosur customs union will meet in Asuncion this week, hoping to edge towards a common position on free trade in the Americas and to overcome a disagreement with Brazil on import financing restrictions.
Presidents of the bloc grouping Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay will meet Thursday while economy and foreign ministers and central bank presidents will hold talks Wednesday.
The leaders of Chile and Bolivia which have free trade agreements with Mercosur will also take part in the Thursday meeting.
Government officials from the four countries started preparatory meetings Sunday and indicated progress had been made on the main issues.

An Argentine diplomat told journalists Tuesday officials had already agreed to set up a working group on the Free Trade Agreement of the Americas (FTAA) which would operate at as high a level as necessary to develop common strategy on the project. The group is expected to start its work next month in Montevideo, the capital of Uruguay.

The timetable for negotiations on the FTAA foresees talks between economy ministry under-secretaries in July, October and January 1998. Those meetings will be followed by a meeting of economy ministers in February and then presidents in March 1998 in Santiago.

At a meeting of trade ministers from across the Americas in Brazil in May, Mercosur frustrated the United States by leaving the issue of how to negotiate the creation of the FTAA until the February meeting.
The heads of state of 34 countries across the Americas met in Miami in December 1994 and agreed to work toward free trade by 2005.

(The co-existence of Mercosur and the FTAA in the future means we must start working now with more intensity, Jose Botafogo Goncalves, the general secretary of economic integration and trade at Brazil's foreign ministry, said last week).

Separately, hopes were running high among Argentine, Uruguayan and Paraguayan officials that they would reach a solution with Brazil on its restrictions on import financing of less than a year introduced in March. Brazil agreed to ease the rules on Mercosur imports until July.

Jorge Campbell, Argentina's subsecretary of trade, told journalists Wednesday the group should introduce a new special regimen for Mercosur imports which would solve the disagreement. It was not immediately clear whether Brazil would be willing to adopt such a regimen for the Mercosur.

Diplomatic sources said there could also be discussion at the meetings of an Argentine plan to introduce a 0.5 percent tariff on imports from non-Mercosur nations. It challenges the Mercosur's policy of common external tariffs.
Additionally, the delegations and leaders are set to discuss increasing trade ties with the European Union, possibly with a view to a free trade pact.
Also high on the agenda will be talks on possible regional link-ups or trade deals between Mercosur and Mexico and the Andean countries of Venezuela, Colombia and Ecuador.
